when: Starting an answer when you need 1–2 seconds to think, without going silent

items.example: That's an interesting question. I've never really thought about it, but I'd say people travel less in winter mainly because of the cost.
items.note: Part 3 mainly; don't use it for every question

items.phrase: I've never really thought about it, but …
items.example: I've never really thought about it, but I suppose I check my watch less now that I always have my phone.

items.phrase: Let me think … / Let me see …
items.example: Let me think … the last time I went to a museum was probably two years ago, on a school trip.
Well, to be completely honest, I don't think I have the patience required to be a teacher.

items.phrase: Off the top of my head, …
items.example: Off the top of my head, I'd say the most popular sport in my country is football, by far.
items.note: = without checking or thinking for long

items.example: How can I put this? It's not that I dislike shopping, it's just that I find crowded malls exhausting.
That's a tricky one, because it really depends on the person's age and lifestyle.

category: Asking the examiner to repeat or clarify
when: When you didn't catch or didn't understand the question

items.phrase: Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
items.example: Sorry, could you repeat the question, please? I didn't quite catch the last part.
items.note: Part 1: the examiner can repeat but not explain

items.example: Sorry, do you mean buildings in my city or tall buildings in general?
I'm not quite sure what you mean by 'national identity' here. Could you rephrase that, please?

items.phrase: If I've understood correctly, you're asking …
items.example: If I've understood correctly, you're asking whether children should choose their own hobbies. Well, …

when: Stating a clear, confident view

items.example: Without a doubt, the living room is the main place where my family gathers every single evening.
Absolutely, I love my hometown because it is where I grew up and made my best childhood memories.
items.note: a strong 'yes' to a Part 1 question

items.example: I'm absolutely convinced that learning a foreign language opens up far more job opportunities.
I firmly believe that children should spend more time outdoors than in front of screens.
There's no question that smartphones have changed the way friends keep in touch.

items.phrase: Personally, I'm a big fan of …
items.example: Personally, I'm a big fan of old buildings because they give a city its character.

when: Giving a softer, balanced opinion (very useful in Part 3, where extreme claims sound weak)

items.example: I would say it is a medium-sized city that is growing very fast because of new businesses.
Generally speaking, older generations prefer to stick to their routines rather than make spontaneous decisions.

items.phrase: As far as I can tell, … / From what I have seen, …
items.example: From what I have seen, country people love outdoor activities like gardening and walking in nature.
I tend to think that people read just as much as before, only on screens instead of paper.
It really depends on whether I prioritise comfort or style at that moment.

items.phrase: I'm not entirely sure, but I'd imagine …
items.example: I'm not entirely sure, but I'd imagine most teenagers in my country spend at least three hours a day online.

items.phrase: To some extent, … / Up to a point, …
items.example: To some extent, advertising helps us discover new products, but it also makes us buy things we don't need.

when: Responding to a statement or a view in a Part 3 question ('Some people say…, do you agree?')

items.example: I couldn't agree more. Children who read for pleasure usually have a much wider vocabulary.

items.phrase: That's true to some extent, but …
items.example: That's true to some extent, but I think online friends can be just as supportive as real ones.

items.phrase: I see what you mean, but …
items.example: I see what you mean, but tall buildings also save a lot of land in crowded cities.

items.phrase: I'm not sure I'd go that far.
items.example: I'm not sure I'd go that far. Social media hasn't replaced face-to-face contact; it's just changed it.

items.phrase: I'm afraid I see it differently.
items.example: I'm afraid I see it differently, because in my country young people actually value tradition a lot.
I'd partly agree with that. Money can buy comfort, but it can't buy close relationships.

when: Explaining why: the second sentence of a Part 1 answer, the core of a Part 3 answer

items.example: I prefer shopping online, mainly because I can compare prices in seconds.
The main reason some people dislike international travel is the stress of being in an unfamiliar place.
The thing is, I work late most evenings, so I rarely have time to cook properly.
This is probably due to the rapid growth of the population in big cities.
Land downtown is extremely expensive, which means developers have to build upward.
items.note: adds a result and shows a complex sentence

items.example: What drives this is mostly the pressure to look successful on social media.
On top of that, the marketing world changes so fast that there is always something new to learn.
items.note: adds a second reason; from the teacher's model answers

when: Supporting an opinion with a specific case (essential in Part 3)

items.example: For instance, my grandparents always plan their days meticulously weeks in advance.
Take my younger brother, for example. He learned most of his English from video games.

items.phrase: A good example of this is …
items.example: A good example of this is the old city centre in my hometown, which is now full of cafés and galleries.
Teenagers spend hours on apps such as TikTok and Instagram.

items.phrase: I can think of a case where …
items.example: I can think of a case where a friend of mine moved abroad and made friends only through a sports club.
To give you an idea, a cup of coffee in the city centre costs almost twice as much as it did five years ago.

when: Questions about change: 'Is it different from the past?', 'How has … changed?', 'Did you … as a child?'

items.example: In the past, you had to live near someone to stay close, whereas nowadays social media keeps friendships alive across countries.
I used to go to the cinema every weekend, but now I mostly stream films at home.
items.note: past habits; don't say 'I am used to go'

items.phrase: Back when I was a kid, …
items.example: Back when I was a kid, we spent the whole summer playing football in the street.
Compared to twenty years ago, people change jobs much more often.

items.phrase: These days, … has become far more …
items.example: These days, online shopping has become far more common than going to physical stores.
items.note: present perfect for change up to now

items.example: Things have changed dramatically since smartphones came along; nobody needs a wristwatch anymore.

items.phrase: There's been a real shift towards …
items.example: There's been a real shift towards eco-friendly cars in the last few years.

when: 'Will … in the future?', 'How might … change?', imaginary situations; vary beyond 'will'

items.phrase: It's (highly) likely that … / … is likely to …
items.example: It's highly likely that most cars will be electric within twenty years.
I'd imagine that future buildings will be covered in plants to help clean the city air.
There's a good chance that robots will take over many routine jobs.
Physical books might well become a luxury item one day.

items.phrase: I can't see … happening (any time soon).
items.example: I can't see online classes replacing schools any time soon, because children need social contact.
If I were to buy a car tomorrow, I would definitely choose a classic black one.
In the long run, working from home could change the way cities are designed.

items.phrase: I'm planning to … / I'm hoping to … / I'd love to …
items.example: I'm hoping to move abroad for my master's degree in a couple of years.

when: Talking about people and society rather than only about yourself (Part 3)

items.phrase: On the whole, … / By and large, …
items.example: By and large, people in my country are very hospitable to guests.
Most people tend to shop online for electronics but still buy food in local markets.
A large number of individuals are naturally night owls and work best late at night.
The younger generation is much more comfortable making plans at the last minute.

items.phrase: In my country, it's quite common to …
items.example: In my country, it's quite common to visit relatives every weekend.
As a rule, elderly people prefer face-to-face conversation to texting.
More often than not, children copy their parents' attitude to reading.

category: Contrasting and showing the other side
when: Adding a contrast in Part 1 (third sentence) or the alternative view in Part 3

items.example: However, I have learned to manage my time better to handle the pressure.
On the other hand, older friends have a lot of life experience and can give you great advice.
While video calls are helpful, they cannot replace real eye contact or body language.
I love living in the city. Having said that, the traffic can be a nightmare.
Even though I love my city, I plan to move abroad soon for my studies.
In contrast, younger professionals often prefer high-rise apartments in the city centre.

items.phrase: It's not that …, it's just that …
items.example: It's not that I dislike sport, it's just that I'd rather watch it than play it.

category: Paraphrasing when you don't know a word
when: You forget or don't know a word. Describe it instead of stopping (LR rewards paraphrase)

items.phrase: It's a kind of … / It's a sort of …
items.example: We stayed in a sort of small wooden house in the mountains, a bit like a cabin.
I always carry a … oh, the thing you use to charge your phone without a socket, a power bank.

items.phrase: I'm not sure what it's called in English, but …
items.example: I'm not sure what it's called in English, but it's a traditional sweet pastry we make for the spring holiday.
She's very… what I mean is, she always notices when someone in the room feels left out.
My uncle is someone who repairs old clocks as a hobby.
items.note: relative clauses are the easiest paraphrase tool

items.phrase: or rather, … / or to put it another way, …
items.example: It was a big building, or rather, a huge shopping complex with offices on top.

when: The first 10–15 seconds of the long turn: name the topic and give background

items.example: I'd like to talk about a hiking trip I had to cancel at the last minute last spring.

items.phrase: The person I'm going to describe is …
items.example: The person I'm going to describe is my aunt, who has an amazing green thumb.
This happened about two years ago, when I was in my final year at school.
I've chosen this place because it's a real hidden gem that most tourists never find.

items.phrase: Let me start by telling you …
items.example: Let me start by telling you where this building is.

items.phrase: There are quite a few … I could talk about, but the one that stands out is …
items.example: There are quite a few gifts I could talk about, but the one that really stands out is a watch my father gave me.

category: Part 2: moving through the bullet points
when: Signposting from one cue-card bullet to the next so the talk sounds organised

items.example: As for what we did there, we mostly wandered around the old town and tried the street food.
Moving on to why I like it so much, it's mainly the peaceful atmosphere.
When it comes to what it looks like, it's a sleek glass tower that stands out against the sky.
Another thing I remember is how cold it was when we left the house at the crack of dawn.
items.note: useful when you glance at your notes

items.example: What made it special was that the whole family was there for the first time in years.

items.phrase: At first …, then …, and in the end …
items.example: At first we were annoyed, then we decided to play it by ear, and in the end we had a great day.
I should also mention that it's completely free to get in, which is quite rare nowadays.

category: Part 2: closing and filling the time
when: The last bullet (why / how you felt) and extending when you still have time

items.example: Looking back, changing the plan was actually a blessing in disguise.
The main reason I like this place is that it lets me escape the hustle and bustle of the city.
It made me realise that you don't need to spend a lot of money to have a memorable day.

items.phrase: If I had the chance, I'd definitely …
items.example: If I had the chance, I'd definitely go back there and stay for at least a week.
items.note: adds a future/hypothetical angle to fill time

items.phrase: Compared to how it was before, …
items.example: Compared to how it was ten years ago, the area is far livelier now.
All in all, that's why that morning will always stick in my mind.

items.phrase: … will always have a special place in my heart.
items.example: That little café will always have a special place in my heart.

when: Cue cards about a friend, family member, famous person, someone who helped you

items.phrase: He/She is the kind of person who …
items.example: She's the kind of person who always remembers your birthday and checks in when you're stressed.

items.phrase: We hit it off straight away.
items.example: We met on the first day of primary school and hit it off straight away.
He's really down-to-earth. Even though he's successful, he never shows off.
Whenever I had problems at home, she was always a shoulder to cry on.

items.phrase: I really look up to him/her because …
items.example: I really look up to my grandfather because he built his business from nothing.
She's in her late forties, quite tall, with short grey hair and a warm smile.

items.phrase: We see eye to eye on most things.
items.example: We see eye to eye on most things, apart from football.

when: Hometown, a place to visit, a building, a quiet or crowded place

items.example: It's tucked away in a small side street behind the main square.
This little park is a real hidden gem; even many locals don't know about it.
The café has a really relaxed atmosphere, so I often go there to study.
From the top floor you get breathtaking views of the whole bay.

items.phrase: to stand out from the crowd / to tower over
items.example: The new tower really stands out from the crowd because of its twisted shape.

items.phrase: It's packed with … / It's always buzzing
items.example: On Friday nights the old town is always buzzing with tourists and street musicians.
My flat is within walking distance of the sea, which is perfect in summer.

when: A gift, a piece of technology, something you own, something you saved for

items.phrase: It's made of … / It's about the size of …
items.example: It's made of dark leather and it's about the size of a paperback book.
My power bank really comes in handy when I'm travelling.
Honestly, my noise-cancelling headphones are something I couldn't live without on public transport.
It's not expensive, but it has huge sentimental value because it belonged to my grandmother.
It cost more than I expected, but it was worth every penny.
It's a sleek, compact laptop that's really user-friendly.

when: Telling a past story (narrative tenses): a trip, a problem, a plan that changed, an early morning

items.phrase: I'll never forget the moment when …
items.example: I'll never forget the moment when the sun came up over the mountains.
We were just leaving the house when my friend called to cancel.
I had never got up that early before, so I set three alarms.
We had to leave at the crack of dawn to catch the first flight.

items.phrase: at the eleventh hour / at the last minute
items.example: The concert was cancelled at the eleventh hour because of the storm.
It turned out that the museum was closed on Mondays, so we had to change our plans.
Seeing the northern lights was a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

when: The 'how you felt' bullet; replace 'happy / sad / good'

items.example: When I found out I'd passed, I was absolutely over the moon.
I was so relieved when the flight finally took off.
I was a bit gutted at first, because I'd been looking forward to the trip for weeks.

items.phrase: It was a real weight off my shoulders.
items.example: Finishing that project was a real weight off my shoulders.
After a weekend in the mountains I felt completely rejuvenated.

items.phrase: nervous / on edge / butterflies in my stomach
items.example: I had butterflies in my stomach before the interview.

items.phrase: It made me feel really proud / appreciated
items.example: Her compliment made me feel really appreciated, because she rarely praises anyone.

when: Part 1 'Do you like…?' / 'What kind of … do you enjoy?' questions

items.phrase: I'm really into … / I'm a big fan of …
items.example: I'm really into science-fiction films, especially ones about space travel.
I'm quite keen on cooking, although I only have time at weekends.
Anything to do with history is right up my street.
I can't get enough of street food when I travel.

items.phrase: I'm not really into … / … isn't really my thing.
items.example: Shopping malls aren't really my thing; I find them too noisy.

items.phrase: I can't stand … / I'm not a big fan of …
items.example: I can't stand waiting in long queues, so I do most of my shopping online.

items.phrase: I prefer … to … / I'd rather … than …
items.pattern: prefer + -ing/noun + to + -ing/noun; would rather + verb + than + verb
items.example: I'd rather read a book than watch TV in the evenings.

when: 'How often do you…?', routines, habits

items.phrase: on a daily basis / every single day
items.example: I use online banking on a daily basis.

items.phrase: once in a while / every now and then
items.example: I go to the cinema once in a while, maybe once every couple of months.
I hardly ever wear a watch these days.
I visit the countryside whenever I get the chance.
I only go to art galleries once in a blue moon.
I make a point of tidying my desk every Friday evening.

items.phrase: It depends on the season / my schedule
items.example: It depends on my schedule, but usually two or three times a week.

when: Use 1–2 per part, naturally and accurately. A forced or misused idiom hurts more than it helps

items.example: I go to my grandparents' village to recharge my batteries after exams.

items.phrase: to escape the hustle and bustle
items.example: Parks let city dwellers escape the hustle and bustle for an hour.
When I'm reading a good novel, I completely lose track of time.
We didn't book anything; we just played it by ear.
Missing that train was a blessing in disguise, because I met an old friend at the station.

items.phrase: to be up in the air
items.example: My summer plans are still up in the air.

items.phrase: the early bird catches the worm
items.example: My dad always says the early bird catches the worm, so he starts work at six.

items.phrase: to burn the candle at both ends
items.example: During exam season, many students burn the candle at both ends.
items.note: from the teacher's Part 3 model answers

items.example: Social media is a double-edged sword: it connects us but also distracts us.

items.phrase: to get on like a house on fire
items.example: My cousin and I got on like a house on fire from the very first day.

when: Adding a point and closing a Part 3 answer in one short sentence

items.example: Furthermore, keeping house plants can drastically improve the air quality inside an apartment.
Ultimately, living in a new country helps people become more independent.
Consequently, punctuality is almost always viewed as a positive trait.
In short, it's a rewarding hobby that benefits both your health and your wallet.
So, all things considered, I think the advantages outweigh the drawbacks.
That's why I'd say that face-to-face communication will never disappear.
